hooks.prompt: Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if you are currently operating as a GRADER (running dimension reviews, computing scores, generating grade reports). If you are NOT in a grading role (e.g. you are an engineer, tester, or debugger), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this restriction only applies to grading sessions. If you ARE the grader, check: graders must ONLY run read-only analysis commands. BLOCK: rm/delete operations, git push/commit/write operations, pip/pip3/uv/poetry/conda/apt install, docker build/push/run, kubectl apply/delete, helm install/upgrade, make, sudo, sed -i, shell output redirection to source files, pytest --cov-report=xml/html (writes files). ALLOW: cat, head, grep, find, ls, wc, stat, git log/diff/status/show, ruff check, mypy, pyright, flake8, pylint, bandit, pytest --collect-only, pytest (without --cov-report to file). Respond {"ok": true} if the command is safe for a grader, or {"ok": false, "reason": "BLOCKED: Graders must only run read-only commands"} if blocked.

Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if you are currently operating as a GRADER (running dimension reviews, computing scores, generating grade reports). If you are NOT in a grading role (e.g. you are an engineer, tester, or debugger), respond {"ok": true} immediately — this restriction only applies to grading sessions. If you ARE the grader, check: the file being written must be a report output file (.md, .json, .html, .txt). Writing source code files (.py, .pyi, .yaml, .yml, .toml, .cfg, .ini, .conf, .sh) is FORBIDDEN for the grader — show fix suggestions as code examples inside the report instead. Respond {"ok": true} if the write is allowed, or {"ok": false, "reason": "BLOCKED: Grader must not write source files"} if blocked.

Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if you are currently operating as a GRADER. If you are NOT in a grading role, respond {"ok": true} immediately. If you ARE the grader, evaluate whether this Bash command is read-only and analysis-focused as required by the grader role. A command is acceptable if it: reads files (cat, head, tail, less, grep, find, ls, wc, stat), runs static analysis tools (mypy, ruff, pyright, flake8, pylint, bandit), or runs pytest in collection-only or non-write mode. A command is NOT acceptable if it: installs packages, writes or modifies files, makes network requests, runs git write operations, or has any persistent side effects. Respond {"ok": true} if the command was read-only and appropriate for a grading session, or {"ok": false, "reason": "<specific description of the inappropriate side effect or write operation>"}.

Context: $ARGUMENTS. FIRST: Determine if this session involved grading a Python codebase (running dimension reviewers, computing scores, generating grade reports). If NO grading work was performed in this session, respond {"ok": true} immediately — this hook only applies to grading sessions.

If grading WAS performed, verify:

1. ALL applicable grading dimensions are present and scored (e.g., correctness, code quality, type safety, test coverage, documentation, security, performance — or a defined subset declared upfront with justification for any omissions).

2. EVERY finding in the report includes ALL four of: (a) the grading dimension it belongs to, (b) a severity level (critical / major / minor / info), (c) a precise file and line reference (file.py:42 format), and (d) a clear description with evidence (the actual code excerpt or tool output that supports the finding).

3. An overall numeric score (e.g., 0-100 or letter grade) is present and its calculation is traceable — the score must be consistent with the individual dimension scores and the severity distribution of findings.

4. The severity distribution is reasonable — a high overall score must not coexist with multiple critical or major findings without explicit justification.

5. The report does not contain placeholder sections, TODO markers, or unfilled template fields.

Respond {"ok": true} if ALL five requirements are satisfied, or {"ok": false, "reason": "<specific description of which requirement is unmet and what must be added or corrected>"}.
